title: Redis Small Examples
description: Use these small Redis examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Store a value under a key
examples.description: A key is a name used to find a value. SET stores a string, and GET reads that string back.
examples.output: SET replies OK. GET returns Garden club.

examples.title: Count with an atomic increment
examples.description: INCR adds one to a key holding an integer.
examples.code:
SET cma:books 0
INCR cma:books
INCR cma:books
GET cma:books

examples.title: Give a key an expiry
examples.description: An expiry makes a key disappear after a time limit.
examples.code:
SET cma:tip "Water the plants" EX 30
TTL cma:tip
examples.output: TTL reports the remaining life in seconds, near 30 if checked immediately.

examples.title: Check whether a key exists
examples.description: EXISTS checks for a key without reading its value.
examples.code:
SET cma:temporary "sample"
EXISTS cma:temporary
DEL cma:temporary
EXISTS cma:temporary
examples.output: The first existence check returns 1, and the final check returns 0.

examples.title: Group fields in a hash
examples.description: A hash stores several named fields under one Redis key.
examples.code:
HSET cma:book:1 title "Moon Trip" pages 60
HGET cma:book:1 title
examples.output: The field lookup returns Moon Trip.

examples.title: Use a list as a small queue
examples.description: A Redis list keeps values in order. Adding on the right and removing on the left gives first-in, first-out behaviour.
examples.code:
DEL cma:queue
RPUSH cma:queue "Moon Trip" "Garden Days"
LPOP cma:queue
examples.output: The removed value is Moon Trip, the first item added.

examples.title: Keep each member once
examples.description: A set holds unique members without a promised order.
examples.code:
DEL cma:readers
SADD cma:readers Mia Sam Mia
SCARD cma:readers

examples.title: Rank values with a sorted set
examples.description: A sorted set pairs each member with a score.
examples.code:
DEL cma:scores
ZADD cma:scores 5 Mia 8 Sam 3 Ravi
ZRANGE cma:scores 0 -1 WITHSCORES
examples.output: The ascending order is Ravi with 3, Mia with 5, then Sam with 8.

examples.title: Scan keys in small batches
examples.description: SCAN walks through key names using a cursor.
examples.output: The response includes a next cursor and some matching keys. Continue with that cursor until it returns 0.

examples.title: Group commands with MULTI
examples.description: MULTI queues commands for EXEC. Redis runs that queued group without another client's commands between them.
examples.code:
MULTI
SET cma:points 2
INCR cma:points
EXEC
examples.output: EXEC returns the results of setting the value and incrementing it to 3.

examples.title: Publish a live message
examples.description: Publish/subscribe sends live messages to clients currently listening to a channel.
examples.code:
# Terminal A:
SUBSCRIBE cma:club-news
# Terminal B:
PUBLISH cma:club-news "Meeting at four"
examples.output: The subscribed terminal receives Meeting at four while it is connected.

examples.title: Choose what must survive a restart
examples.description: Redis persistence settings decide how data is written to disk.
examples.code:
Example decision:
Cached book summary: can be loaded again if lost.
Only copy of a payment record: must not depend on an unreviewed cache setup.
Check the server's RDB snapshot and AOF settings, then test a practice restart.
examples.output: The worked decision separates replaceable cache data from records that need stronger guarantees.
